changelog.summary: Server-created wallets (decane-node 1.5.0 createUser): nothing to configure. A wallet the app's server made is opened by the person's first sign-in through the returning-user path (provision on the JWT). If POST /share answers 409 WALLET_EXISTS mid-creation (the server created the wallet a moment after the sign-in said there was none), the generated key is discarded unused and the wallet that exists is opened; a new WalletExistsError is exported but never reaches callers. Update before enabling server-side creation for a project: an older client would fail its own creation with an error in that race.

The identity tier: protection: 'identity' (deferDeviceProtection is now an alias) — no passkey, no password, no recovery file; nothing stored on the device; every visit is a sign-in and the enclave provisions a fresh share against it. Security statement in the spec. Existing users port on their next sign-in with the same wallet (enrolled wallets silently; an unenrolled wallet with a wrapped share on the device sees one last prompt, then 'migrated-to-identity'). resumeSessionAcrossTabs defaults to true in that tier. Wallet creation now WAITS for the enclave to enrol the wallet (provisional server share, three attempts) and throws WalletEnrolmentError leaving nothing behind, in every tier. A 429 on provisioning is ProvisioningRateLimitedError, never NewDeviceError; EnclaveHttpError carries any other enclave status. Session renewal now applies to ordinary wallet sessions (2.26 armed it only for connectWithAccessToken sessions). Passkey entry points refuse in the identity tier; protectDevice() is a no-op there.

Sessions: the access token lasts eight hours (was two) and is renewed at 75% of its life while the user is active, via POST /auth/refresh, capped at seven days; 'session-renewed' event. resumeSessionAcrossTabs (opt-in, and exposed on <DecaneKit> as of this release): the live session resumes in a new tab rather than only after a reload. Return visits are faster: attestation collateral is cached in localStorage for 12 hours and a verified attestation persists for the tab, so the enclave is not re-verified on every unlock.

signMessage on an EVM or Tron chain given a Uint8Array now decodes the bytes to the string the enclave hashes (lossless for UTF-8, which every hex personal_sign a dApp sends — SIWE included — is) and throws CallSequenceError for bytes that are not UTF-8. Before, the bytes went into the JSON body as an object and the signer refused them — which the EIP-1193 provider's personal_sign path hit for every hex message. Solana is unchanged (raw bytes).

Handing a session between apps of one project: connectWithAccessToken(token) / useSocialAuth().signInWithAccessToken(token) adopts a Decane access token another app handed over (in a URL), signed in at once and unlocked on the first signature — with deferDeviceProtection that prompts for nothing; the session lasts as long as the token and ends with session-expired. Everything the client persists (identity, last signed-out user, live session) is now keyed by the app id rather than the API key, so two apps of one project under different keys on one origin see the same signed-in user and a same-tab navigation between them resumes the full session; entries written under the old key are read once and moved. New InvalidAccessTokenError (INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN).

Deferred wallet protection: deferDeviceProtection (DecaneConnectConfig and SocialConfig) makes sign-in ask for no passkey or password — the wallet is created and the session opens with no stored device share — and the new protectDevice() wraps and stores one later, at the app's own moment (before the first transaction, say): passkey where the device can hold one, otherwise promptUnlockPassword. Resolves false on a dismissed prompt rather than throwing. deviceProtected() reports whether this device holds a wrapped share. Both on useSocialWallet(). Until protected, a device has no passkey/password unlock and every visit is a full sign-in; recovery is unchanged. The server's wallet_created event records unlockMethod "deferred".

Signing back in after sign-out: disconnect() now remembers WHICH account signed out (a userId, a lookup key and not a credential), so canSignInWithPasskey()/canUnlockWithPassword() and their sign-in twins offer that account's own passkey or password back even when several accounts are enrolled on one browser — previously, with more than one enrolled, the kit refused to guess and both read false. New forgetLastUser() is "use a different account": drops the memory, leaves device shares untouched; on useSocialWallet() it also recomputes canUsePasskey. connect()/unlock() keep the strict lookup. The llms.txt hook references were also brought up to the real return shapes (31 members were missing, across passkey, password, recovery, typed-data, balances and access token).

Phone-number sign-in via SMS (Termii). connectWithPhone(phone) + verifyPhoneCode(phone, code), 'phone' in authMethods, and a phone form in both built-in UIs. Numbers must be E.164 (+2348012345678) — local formats are rejected rather than guessed at, because the wallet is derived from the number and inferring a country would merge two users onto one wallet or split one across two. Identity is HMAC(E.164), so a phone user is a DIFFERENT user from the same human's email or Google sign-in, exactly as email and Google already differ. Available in all three SDKs.

Sign-in now returns the provider's profile: ConnectResult gains an optional `profile` of { name?, email?, picture? }, so apps can greet the user by name instead of by address. It is passed through from the verified Google or KingsChat response and never stored — the backend keeps only an HMAC and a masked identifier — so it is available at sign-in and nowhere else. Absent entirely for email sign-in. Expo SDK 0.2.0 has the same field. useSocialAuth() exposes it as `profile`, null until a sign-in returns one and not restored across reloads.

KingsChat sign-in now requests only the profile scope by default, in both the web and Expo SDKs. It previously asked for send_chat_message, which put 'post as you' on a consent screen whose only job is to log the user in. Pass `scopes` explicitly if your app actually sends chat messages.

React Native / Expo SDK released as decane-connect-kit-expo (see llms-expo.txt). Server-assisted recovery is now always on — a user who reinstalls gets their wallet back from signing in alone, so the serverAssistedRecovery option was removed. Google sign-in on mobile uses an in-app auth sheet needing nothing registered in Google Cloud. Adds connectWithGoogleToken() so native Google Sign-In resolves to the SAME wallet as the web redirect flow, and connectWithKingsChat().

Optional per-signature authority: requireAssertionPerSignature makes every signature need a fresh passkey assertion, verified inside the TEE against a single-use 60s challenge, instead of an unlocked session signing freely until expiry. The session still stays warm — this does NOT shorten sessionDurationMinutes. Available on both DecaneConnectConfig and SocialConfig. Default false, so existing behaviour is unchanged. Requires TEE signer v0.2.3+.

Custom auth: sign in with a JWT from your own issuer (Auth0, Clerk, Firebase, Cognito, or your own backend). Adds DecaneConnect.connectWithToken(token, opts?), SocialConfig.customAuth, and useSocialAuth().signInWithToken / .signInWithCustomAuth. Backward compatible — no existing API changed.
Baseline for this manifest. Wallet connect (EVM, Solana, Tron, Bitcoin) plus non-custodial social sign-in via Google and email, TEE-backed signing, 2-of-3 Shamir recovery.
Ports web 2.28.0: a 409 WALLET_EXISTS from POST /share mid-creation falls through to provisioning the wallet the app's server created. Update before enabling server-side creation for a project.

Ports the identity tier from web 2.27.0: protection: 'identity' establishes no unlock tier at creation — no passkey ceremony, no biometric key, no PIN, nothing in the keystore — and provisions from the enclave on every visit; canUnlock/hasPasskey/canSignInWithPasskey false, passkey entry points throw CALL_SEQUENCE, activeUnlockMethod null. Existing users port on their next sign-in (enrolled silently; a legacy unenrolled wallet with a stored share sees its tier's prompt once, then 'migrated-to-identity'). Creation waits for enrolment in every tier (WALLET_ENROLMENT_FAILED, nothing left behind). PROVISIONING_RATE_LIMITED for a 429 on provisioning; ENCLAVE_HTTP carries other statuses. Session renewal: the access token (eight hours) is renewed at 75% of its life while the app holds a live identity ('session-renewed'), which this package lacked entirely; the device unlock token remains the way back once a token has lapsed on the device tier.

X (Twitter) sign-in: connectWithX() and 'x' in authMethods, the same in-app sheet and redirect as Google; profile carries the handle as username (X releases no email). Session renewal: the access token lasts two hours with no refresh token, so a device on the secure-enclave or PIN tier now holds a 90-day device unlock token (issued at creation/provisioning, stored beside the share under the same key) and unlock() redeems it with the device's own biometric or PIN — no email code; canUnlock() says whether it can, removeDeviceUnlock() is the lost-phone switch, UNLOCK_TOKEN_REJECTED names a refused token. addPasskey()/hasPasskey(): move a device from the enclave or PIN tier to a passkey after signing in with email, Google or X. getEthereumProvider(): the web SDK's EIP-1193 provider, for viem / wagmi / ethers.

Rebuilt against the current infra/tee-measurement.json. 0.3.0 shipped the enclave measurement captured against signer 0.1.3, so every sign-in and unlock() against the live signer (0.2.10+, measurement fb14dc13…) failed with AttestationError "TEE measurement not accepted". The previous measurement is retained as a second accepted entry, exactly as in decane-connect-kit 2.22+. No API change. Also: signMessage on EVM/Tron given a Uint8Array now decodes UTF-8 bytes to the string the enclave hashes and refuses non-UTF-8 bytes (CallSequenceError), instead of sending an object the signer rejected.

Server-side user and wallet creation: createUser(identifier, { createWallet?, metadata? }) and createUserWallet(userId) with the project secret (POST /v1/app/users, POST /v1/app/users/:id/wallet). The enclave creates the key; the person's first sign-in opens it. Per-project opt-in (SERVER_WALLETS_DISABLED until switched on). New codes INVALID_IDENTIFIER, WALLET_EXISTS, WALLET_FROZEN, ENCLAVE_UNAVAILABLE, RETRY_LATER; a user.wallet_created webhook.

Spec correction, no package change: access tokens last 8 hours (not ~30 minutes / 2 hours) and are renewable through POST /auth/refresh with the still-valid token as Bearer, capped at 7 days from sign-in; and there is NO per-IP rate limit on the auth endpoints — the old '20 requests / 15 minutes per IP' claim was wrong. OTP attempts are limited per target address (10 / 15 min), code sends at 3 / hour / address.

Per-user records, the replacement for Privy's custom metadata. Every user carries two flat JSON records (strings, numbers, booleans; ≤100 keys, ≤32 KB): `preferences`, the user's own choices, written with THEIR access token (getPreferences / updatePreferences / setPreferences, backed by GET/PATCH/PUT /me/preferences); and `metadata`, the app's facts about them, written only with the new `projectSecret` option (dck_sk_…, env DECANE_PROJECT_SECRET) by user id (getUserMetadata / updateUserMetadata / setUserMetadata, plus the same trio for preferences) and read-only to the user (getMetadata), so an entitlement may live there. A patch merges and null removes a key. New error codes INVALID_RECORD, NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED.

Base URL resolution treats an empty value as unset at every step (apiBase option, DECANE_API_BASE env, then the built-in https://backend.decane.app). Deploy templates that write `DECANE_API_BASE: ${DECANE_API_BASE:-}` land an empty string, which 1.3.0 took as the base and sent every request to a relative URL ("Failed to parse URL from /share/addresses"). The resolved base is now readable as client.apiBase.
Server-side phone sign-in: connectWithPhone(phone) + verifyPhoneCode(phone, code), mirroring the email OTP pair. New SMS_NOT_CONFIGURED error code for deployments with no SMS provider.

Server-side sign-in: connectWithEmail/verifyEmailCode (email OTP), connectWithGoogleToken, connectWithKingsChatToken, connectWithToken (custom auth), getKingsChatConfig, revokeAccessToken. New `apiKey` option (env DECANE_API_KEY) and DecaneApiError with backend error codes. DecaneAddresses gains `tron`; DecaneLinkedAccount.chainType widens to include "tron" — exhaustive switches need a tron arm. Verify-only usage is unchanged and still needs no apiKey.
Baseline: verifyAccessToken (static ES256 key or JWKS), safeVerifyAccessToken, getAddresses, getUser, standalone verifyAccessToken.

connect.$comment: Server-to-server provisioning API for agencies/builders: one project + API key per end-client. Path-versioned, not package-versioned.

changelog.summary: Several sign-in callbacks per key: callback_urls[] on POST /clients, POST /clients/:ref/keys and PATCH /clients/:ref/keys/:keyId (replaced whole, like allowed_origins), and on key rows. /auth/google/init and /auth/x/init pick the entry whose host matches the request's Origin (or Referer) — exact host with port first, then hostname — and fall back to the first entry, so one key serves an app from its domain, a preview host and localhost. The single callback_url is still accepted everywhere and reported as the first entry.

Initial release. Organization tier above projects, with org-scoped provisioning tokens (dck_org_) minted from the dashboard's Organization page. POST /connect/v1/clients creates a client's project and first API key in one transaction, idempotent on your own external_ref. Keys minted here are origin_policy=strict: a non-empty allowed_origins list is required and a request carrying neither Origin nor Referer is refused, closing the replay of a key scraped from a published bundle. Deprovision archives AND revokes every key; there is no hard-delete, because destroying a project cascades to end users' wallet shares.

First release: the Python port of decane-node 1.5.0. Sync DecaneClient and async AsyncDecaneClient over httpx; verification with a static key or the JWKS (PyJWT); server-side sign-in (email, phone, Google token, KingsChat token, custom auth); per-user records; server-side user and wallet creation. Deviations: a JWKS fetch failure is NETWORK_ERROR not an auth error, snake_case names, 15 s default timeout, a bad verification key fails at construction.

First release: the Rust port of decane-node 1.5.0. Async on tokio, reqwest with rustls; verification with a static key or the JWKS (jsonwebtoken); server-side sign-in (email, phone, Google token, KingsChat token, custom auth); per-user records; server-side user and wallet creation. Deviations: a JWKS fetch failure is NetworkError not an auth error, snake_case names, 15 s default timeout, a bad verification key fails at build(), ApiErrorCode::Other for unknown codes.

First release of the Swift SDK for iOS 16+ / macOS 13+, on the shared Rust wallet core (UniFFI, XCFramework on the GitHub release). The identity tier: email, phone, Google-token, KingsChat-token and custom-token sign-in; wallet creation and enrolment; provisioning, including wallets a server created with createUser; signing for EVM (messages, transactions, EIP-712, EIP-7702), Solana and Tron; session resume and refresh; events. Not yet: the device tier, passkeys, redirect sign-in, recovery files (each answers a clear error).
